result.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
result.summary: \emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a \emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup. Because the random mapping is not learned from language, its prompts can be highly unnatural, and as such easily detectable through input guardrails, and the risk estimates they yield are not grounded in natural prompts. In this paper, we demonstrate that the same continuous latent-space framework can be coupled directly to a learned generative distribution over language, a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), which removes the artificial random mapping while preserving the standard-Gaussian latent formulation and the downstream sampling or optimization procedure. We evaluate this approach under two settings: sampling-based estimation using \emph{RareTrap} and optimization-based search using \emph{ThinkTrap}. We find that character-level perplexity drops from $10^3$--$10^7$ to 3--5 in RareTrap and from 20--28 to 4.3--5.4 in ThinkTrap. We also find that model risk estimates can differ by an order of magnitude across the two mappings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把黑盒攻击的连续高斯隐空间框架接到连续扩散语言模型（dLLM）上，用学习到的语言分布替代随机映射解码，在 RareTrap 采样与 ThinkTrap 优化两种设置下生成攻击提示（如诱发 overthinking），并比较两种映射下字符级困惑度与风险估计的差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「隐向量到文本」解码器的选择直接决定产物的自然度与下游估计，可供核查 latent 表示解码保真度、隐空间搜索构造证据等线索；诱发 overthinking 亦与 THINK/STOP 长度预算相关，但非视觉推理，迁移需自行判断。
